# The distributions7 package {#sec-distributions7}

@sec-links dealt with the transformation of a single number; this chapter
deals with the object that transformation serves, a parametric family of
probability distributions carrying its density together with everything a
modelling routine needs to know about it.

The chapter divides into four parts, which can be read in order or separately.
@sec-distributions sets out what a `distrib` object provides and develops the
likelihood theory the package rests on — score, observed and expected
information, the Bartlett identities in full generality, derivatives
transported onto the unconstrained scale by Faà di Bruno's formula,
derivatives with respect to the response, and derivatives of the distribution
function, which censored likelihoods require — and then presents the fourteen
families.

@sec-transformations treats **operators on distributions**: a change of
variables, zero-inflation, zero-adjustment and truncation, each of which takes
a distribution and returns another with the same machinery intact. The
derivatives of the constructed model must be assembled from those of its
parent, and doing so at fourth order in full generality requires some
combinatorics of set partitions.

@sec-fitting applies the apparatus to the simplest problem that exercises all
of it, maximum likelihood for an i.i.d. sample. @sec-fallbacks describes what
a distribution receives when it implements nothing but its density, which is
the part of the package that makes user-defined families practical.
